task_3.title: Prevent caching partial wheel downloads
task_3.description: Wheel downloads should only become visible in the cache after the full download has completed successfully. This prevents interrupted or failed downloads from leaving partially written wheel files that can later be reused as if they were valid cached artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that partially downloaded wheel files are not stored or reused as completed cache entries when a download is interrupted or fails.

expectation.grounded: The download_file helper must make the target destination observable only after the response stream has been fully written successfully. If response iteration or writing fails before completion, the destination path must not contain the partially written wheel as a completed cached file, and normal failure signaling should be preserved.
expectation.conceptual: Downloads should be all-or-nothing from the user's perspective: a completed cache entry must represent a complete downloaded file, while failed or interrupted downloads must not leave corrupted artifacts behind.

constraints.grounded: Keep the existing download_file behavior for successful downloads, including streamed chunk handling and progress behavior. Do not suppress or transform download failures solely to clean up partial output. The fix must apply to wheel files and other artifacts downloaded through the same helper path without changing the public download contract.
constraints.conceptual: Successful downloads should continue to behave the same, and failures should still be visible to callers. The only intended change is preventing incomplete files from being treated as valid cached downloads.

behavior: Completed downloads still write the full response body to the requested destination.
A failed or interrupted download no longer leaves the destination populated with the bytes that happened to be written before failure.
The final cached file becomes visible only after all streamed chunks have been written successfully.
Download errors remain observable to the caller instead of being hidden by the partial-file cleanup behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a wheel download completes successfully, when the caller checks the destination afterward, it should contain the complete downloaded wheel.
Given a wheel download is interrupted before the response stream finishes, when the operation fails, it should not leave a partially written wheel at the final cache destination.
When a streaming or write error occurs during a download, it should still be reported through the existing failure path while avoiding a completed-looking cache artifact.
When existing successful download flows use progress reporting or chunked streaming, they should continue to behave as before.

task_2.title: Disable wheel content validation during install
task_2.description: Poetry 1.5.1 changes wheel installation so that RECORD-based content validation is skipped while installing a wheel. This is a temporary workaround for out-of-memory failures seen with large wheels, while retaining the surrounding wheel validation and installation flow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing packages from large wheel files does not fail or exhaust memory because the installer validates every wheel file's contents during installation.

expectation.grounded: During `WheelInstaller.install`, wheel RECORD validation should be invoked with content validation disabled so installation does not perform full per-file content checks. `_WheelFileValidationError` handling should remain in place for validation issues still reported by RECORD validation, and installation should continue through the existing wheel install flow.
expectation.conceptual: When a user installs a package from a wheel, the installer should avoid expensive content verification that can make large wheels unusable, while preserving normal handling for other wheel validation problems.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove RECORD validation entirely, do not bypass `_WheelFileValidationError` capture for non-content validation issues, and do not change the normal wheel installation path beyond disabling content validation.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should reduce memory pressure for large wheels without broadly weakening unrelated validation behavior or altering successful installation semantics.

behavior: Wheel installation no longer validates the contents of every file listed in a wheel's RECORD during install.
Large wheels that previously risked out-of-memory failures during content validation can proceed through installation without that validation step.
Wheel validation still runs in a reduced mode, so validation failures not dependent on file content checks can still be captured and reported through the existing invalid-wheel mechanism.
The change affects installation-time behavior only; it does not introduce a new user-facing command or configuration option.
acceptance_criteria: When a package is installed from a large wheel, it should not perform full RECORD content validation as part of installation.
When a wheel would only fail because of content validation, installation should not be blocked by that content-validation failure.
When RECORD validation reports a non-content wheel issue, the installer should preserve the existing invalid-wheel handling behavior.
When a valid wheel is installed, it should continue through the normal installation flow with no new user action or configuration required.

task_1.title: Speed up dependency resolver backtracking
task_1.description: Dependency resolution now avoids repeated work in high-backtracking scenarios by preserving reusable resolver cache state across still-active decision levels. The change is intended to make conflict-heavy updates much faster while preserving the same dependency resolution outcomes and candidate selection semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution remains correct but runs substantially faster for projects whose version solving requires many backtracking steps, especially when conflicting packages have many available versions.

expectation.grounded: During version solving, DependencyCache.search_for should reuse dependency search results for the same package identity and source metadata across solver decision levels, filtering cached candidates against the active dependency constraint and falling back to provider search when the filtered cached result cannot satisfy the request. VersionSolver backtracking should retain DependencyCache entries and contradicted incompatibility records from decision levels that remain active, while removing entries associated with reverted decision levels.
expectation.conceptual: When the resolver backtracks, it should keep reusable knowledge that is still valid instead of starting over, so repeated dependency lookups and conflict deductions are avoided without changing the selected dependency solution or failure outcome.

constraints.grounded: Cache reuse must continue to distinguish dependency identity by complete package name and source attributes, must respect the current version constraint on every lookup, must preserve provider behavior for cases such as pre-release fallback when no cached candidate remains eligible, and must not keep contradicted incompatibilities or dependency candidates from decision levels that have been rolled back.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must not broaden or narrow accepted dependency versions, mix candidates from different sources, leak stale conflict state after backtracking, or change user-visible resolution results.

behavior: Backtracking no longer clears all dependency search cache entries; it removes only entries introduced at solver decision levels that are being rolled back.
Backtracking no longer clears all contradicted incompatibility information; it removes only contradiction records introduced at rolled-back decision levels.
Dependency candidate lookups can reuse candidate lists collected at earlier still-active decision levels and filter them according to the current dependency constraint.

When a cached candidate list does not leave any eligible candidates for the current constraint, the resolver performs a fresh provider lookup so provider-level candidate selection semantics are preserved.
Resolver preference and package selection paths use the decision-level-aware dependency cache, reducing repeated provider searches and repeated constraint evaluation during heavy backtracking.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency resolution that repeatedly backtracks across many candidate versions, when earlier decision levels remain valid, the resolver should reuse dependency lookup and contradicted-incompatibility information from those levels instead of discarding it wholesale.
When the resolver rolls back from a higher decision level to a lower one, information introduced only in the rolled-back levels should no longer influence later solving decisions.

When a dependency is looked up with a narrower or different version constraint than a cached lookup, the returned candidates should satisfy the active constraint and should not include candidates solely because they were present in the cached broader lookup.

When cached candidates for a dependency do not satisfy the active request, dependency lookup should fall back to the normal provider behavior rather than reporting an empty candidate set solely because of cache filtering.

For the same project and requested operation, the final resolved solution or resolution failure should remain the same as before the optimization, while high-backtracking scenarios complete with significantly less repeated work.

task_4.title: Preserve relative script paths in poetry run
task_4.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes a regression where running scripts via relative paths through poetry run could fail because the command path was normalized before being passed to process execution. Relative executable names that include path syntax, such as current-directory script invocations, should remain intact while Poetry continues to resolve environment-managed executables normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that poetry run can execute scripts referenced by relative paths without losing the relative path prefix needed by the operating system to locate the script.

expectation.grounded: When Env.get_command_from_bin receives a non-pip executable name, it should return a command list whose executable entry preserves the original unresolved command string when the command is not found in Poetry's configured script directories. Env._bin should return a subprocess-ready string rather than a path object, while public path-oriented accessors such as Env.python, Env.pip, and pip command checks should continue to use path semantics where existence checks or path values are required.
expectation.conceptual: Running a command through Poetry with an explicit relative script path should behave the same as invoking that relative path directly in a shell: the path text should not be simplified in a way that changes executable resolution.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing behavior for pip handling, embedded pip fallback, Python executable access, resolved executables located in environment script directories, and NullEnv command pass-through. Do not alter non-pip command resolution beyond preserving unresolved command strings exactly enough for subprocess execution semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to command execution path handling and must not regress normal environment executable lookup or pip invocation behavior.

behavior: Relative non-pip commands passed to poetry run, including commands with an explicit current-directory prefix, remain subprocess command strings instead of being normalized as filesystem paths.
If a requested executable is found in Poetry's environment script directories or environment path location, Poetry still returns the resolved executable path as the command to run.

If a requested executable is not found in those managed locations, Poetry passes through the original command text so operating-system subprocess resolution sees the same path expression the user provided.
Path-based consumers of Env._bin results continue converting to path values before performing existence checks or returning path-oriented properties.
Pip command construction continues to use the embedded pip fallback when needed and the module-based pip invocation otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project environment and an executable argument like ./foo.py that is not resolved from Poetry's managed script directories, when poetry run prepares the command, then the executable argument should remain ./foo.py rather than being reduced to foo.py.
When poetry run receives a relative path script with explicit path syntax, it should pass a command to process execution that preserves the user's relative path semantics.
When a non-pip executable is found in the environment's script directory, Poetry should continue to invoke the resolved executable path.
When pip is requested, Poetry should continue to use its existing pip command selection behavior, including embedded pip fallback when pip is unavailable in the environment.
When code accesses the environment's Python or pip path properties, those values should remain usable as filesystem paths.

task_6.title: Resolve transitive prerelease dependencies
task_6.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes dependency resolution cases where a transitive dependency could only be satisfied by a prerelease version, but cached candidate results caused the solver to report no solution. The resolver should now re-evaluate narrowed dependency constraints so prerelease candidates are considered when no non-prerelease candidates remain, while preserving normal prerelease selection rules.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution can find a valid solution when a transitive dependency is progressively constrained to require a prerelease package version and no non-prerelease version satisfies the final constraint.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry's solver evaluates a Dependency through DependencyCache.search_for and a previously cached candidate list is narrowed by the current version constraint to no allowed DependencyPackage entries, it must perform a fresh provider lookup for that Dependency so the normal prerelease fallback behavior can apply. This must allow solve operations to succeed for transitive constraints where the only satisfying candidate is a prerelease, instead of raising a solver failure caused by stale cached stable-only candidates.
expectation.conceptual: The dependency resolver should treat prerelease versions as eligible fallback candidates whenever a dependency, including one introduced transitively, has no stable versions that satisfy all active constraints. Resolution should not fail solely because an earlier, broader lookup cached candidates before the stricter constraint was known.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the general prerelease policy: prerelease versions should remain excluded unless explicitly allowed or unless no non-prerelease versions satisfy the active dependency constraint. Cached dependency results must remain consistent across constraint narrowing and solver backtracking, preserving usable candidates from still-active decision levels while discarding only entries from rolled-back levels.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing stable-version preference and solver behavior intact for ordinary dependencies. The fix should only affect cases where cached resolution state would otherwise hide the only valid prerelease candidate or survive after it is no longer valid.

behavior: A cached candidate set for a dependency is filtered against the currently requested version constraint before being reused.
If filtering cached candidates leaves no allowed versions, the resolver performs a new dependency search rather than treating the empty filtered cache as authoritative.
The refreshed search can surface prerelease candidates under the existing rule that prereleases are considered when no stable candidates satisfy the constraint.
A valid transitive dependency graph whose only final candidate for a package is a prerelease should resolve successfully instead of producing a no-solution solver error.
Dependency cache entries are tracked by solver decision level so backtracking removes cache entries from rolled-back levels without invalidating earlier still-relevant cached results.
acceptance_criteria: Given a root dependency graph where a package is first considered under a broad constraint and later constrained transitively so that all stable candidates are excluded, when a prerelease version satisfies the later constraint, then dependency solving should select that prerelease and complete successfully.
When cached candidates for a dependency no longer satisfy the active constraint, it should re-query available candidates and apply the normal prerelease fallback behavior.
When at least one non-prerelease candidate satisfies the active dependency constraint, prerelease candidates should not be preferred merely because this cache fix is present.

When the solver backtracks across decision levels, cached dependency results from reverted levels should not affect later candidate searches, while still-valid earlier cache entries may continue to be reused.

task_7.title: Correct cached repository package parsing
task_7.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes repository package metadata extraction when HTTP responses are cached. CacheControl file-cache entries represent the full HTTP response rather than the package archive alone, so treating those files as wheels or source archives could cause package dependencies to be missed during resolution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages from HTTP repositories are parsed from valid package artifacts even when their responses are cached, so their declared dependencies are not ignored.

expectation.grounded: HTTPRepository package metadata retrieval must not parse CacheControl FileCache entries as wheel or source archive files. When package metadata is needed for a repository link, the artifact made available for inspection must contain the actual distribution content, and dependency metadata must remain visible even when the package URL has an existing CacheControl cache entry. Authenticator must not provide URL-derived CacheControl cache file paths as package artifact paths for this flow.
expectation.conceptual: Resolving or installing packages from HTTP repositories should produce the same dependency information whether the underlying HTTP response was cached or freshly retrieved. Cache storage files must never be mistaken for installable package files.

constraints.grounded: Do not reintroduce behavior that treats cachecontrol's URL-derived cache files as distribution archives or bypasses valid artifact retrieval for repository metadata inspection. Existing repository authentication, certificate handling, and general HTTP response caching behavior should remain otherwise unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve correctness for cached repository packages without changing unrelated repository access, security configuration, or dependency resolution behavior.

behavior: HTTP repository package inspection no longer yields CacheControl file-cache paths as package files.
A package URL that already exists in the HTTP response cache is still inspected from actual distribution content.
Dependencies declared by cached repository packages are preserved in the package metadata used by resolution.
The authenticator no longer participates in package retrieval by exposing a cached file path for an arbitrary URL.
Download-related repository behavior is tied to obtaining a usable package artifact rather than copying or parsing cache bookkeeping files.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package URL whose HTTP response has been cached, when Poetry inspects that package from an HTTP repository, it should read metadata from the actual package artifact rather than from the cache entry.
When a cached repository package declares dependencies, those dependencies should be present in the package metadata used during dependency resolution.
When the same repository package is processed with and without an existing HTTP cache entry, the parsed dependency set should be equivalent.
When package metadata is retrieved through the repository and authenticator flow, CacheControl file-cache paths should not be exposed or consumed as package artifact paths.
Existing authentication credentials, repository certificate configuration, and normal HTTP response caching should continue to operate independently of this parsing fix.

task_5.title: Fix in-project virtualenv dependency installation
task_5.description: The update corrects Poetry's handling of in-project virtual environments so dependency installation and environment discovery do not treat a configured in-project environment as already existing unless the project-local environment directory is actually present and allowed by configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency operations for in-project virtual environments only reuse a project-local environment when it actually exists, while still allowing Poetry to create and use in-project environments according to the user's configuration.

expectation.grounded: Environment resolution and environment listing must distinguish the user's in-project virtualenv preference from the existence of a reusable project-local virtual environment. The virtualenvs.in-project setting should continue to control whether in-project environments are enabled, disabled, or inferred, but an environment should be returned as an existing project-local virtualenv only when that environment directory exists and the setting is not explicitly false.
expectation.conceptual: Poetry should install dependencies into the correct in-project virtual environment without mistaking configuration intent for an already-created environment. Existing project-local environments should be discovered when appropriate, and nonexistent ones should not be reported or reused as if they were present.

constraints.grounded: When virtualenvs.in-project is explicitly false, an existing project-local virtual environment must not be selected or included in environment listings. When the setting is unset, an existing project-local virtual environment must still be detected. When the setting is explicitly true but the project-local virtual environment directory is absent, environment discovery must not return it as an existing environment.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress the supported configuration modes: users who disable in-project environments should not have them picked up, users with an existing local environment should keep that environment recognized, and users enabling local environments should not have missing environments treated as usable.

behavior: Environment resolution now returns the project-local virtual environment only if that environment directory exists and in-project virtual environments have not been explicitly disabled.
Environment listing now includes the project-local virtual environment only if it exists and is not disabled by configuration.

The decision to use in-project virtual environments remains true when virtualenvs.in-project is explicitly true, false when explicitly false, and inferred from the local environment directory when unset.
An explicitly enabled but not-yet-created in-project virtual environment is no longer treated as an existing environment during resolution or listing.
acceptance_criteria: Given virtualenvs.in-project is true and the project-local virtual environment does not yet exist, when Poetry resolves the current environment, it should not return a nonexistent project-local environment as an existing one.
Given virtualenvs.in-project is true and the project-local virtual environment exists, when Poetry resolves or lists environments, it should select or include that project-local environment.
Given virtualenvs.in-project is unset and the project-local virtual environment exists, when Poetry resolves or lists environments, it should detect and include the project-local environment.
Given virtualenvs.in-project is false, when Poetry resolves or lists environments, it should ignore the project-local virtual environment even if its directory exists.

When installing dependencies for a project configured to use an in-project virtual environment, Poetry should install into a valid environment rather than treating a missing project-local environment as already usable.

task_9.title: Reduce memory use when installing large wheels
task_9.description: Wheel installation was adjusted so that very large wheel archives no longer consume excessive memory during validation. The installer should continue to perform the normal installation flow while avoiding the expensive content-validation step that caused out-of-memory behavior for large wheels.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing large wheel packages does not consume excessive memory or fail due to the wheel content validation performed before installation.

expectation.grounded: During wheel installation, the WheelInstaller install flow should still open the wheel, run RECORD validation through WheelFile validation, and proceed with installation, but content validation of wheel payload files must be disabled so large wheels are not fully read into memory for that validation step. Non-content WheelFileValidationError outcomes should continue to be captured as invalid wheel issues.
expectation.conceptual: Installing a valid large wheel should complete without excessive memory usage caused by pre-install content checks, while preserving the existing handling of wheel metadata or record validation problems.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to disabling wheel payload content validation during the install-time RECORD validation path; the installer should not remove the surrounding wheel validation attempt, invalid-wheel issue tracking, or normal package installation behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve memory behavior for large packages without weakening unrelated installation behavior or changing how non-content wheel validity problems are surfaced.

behavior: Installing a wheel no longer performs content validation for each payload file as part of the pre-install RECORD validation step.
Large wheels should avoid the high memory consumption previously triggered by validating wheel contents before installation.
The installer still attempts RECORD validation before invoking the normal wheel installation process.
Validation failures that are not dependent on payload content checking continue to be recorded as invalid wheel issues.
acceptance_criteria: When a large valid wheel is installed, it should install without excessive memory consumption from pre-install content validation.
When wheel RECORD validation runs during installation, it should skip payload content checking while retaining the remaining validation behavior.
When non-content wheel validation detects an invalid wheel condition, the installer should continue to record that invalid wheel issue as before.
When installing ordinary valid wheels, the package installation behavior should remain unchanged apart from the skipped content-validation work.

task_8.title: Respect explicit dependency sources during resolution
task_8.description: Dependency resolution now prevents a direct-origin package from satisfying a dependency that explicitly asks for a repository source unless that direct-origin package fully satisfies the dependency. This fixes cases where an explicit source could be ignored and a URL, VCS, path, or other direct-origin candidate with a matching version was selected instead.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependencies declaring an explicit source are resolved from that source and are not incorrectly satisfied by same-named direct-origin dependencies just because their versions match.

expectation.grounded: When Provider.search_for evaluates a dependency that has a cached direct-origin package candidate, it should return that direct-origin package only if the package satisfies the dependency as a whole. If the direct-origin candidate does not satisfy the dependency, including when the dependency names an explicit source that the direct-origin package does not match, resolution should continue through the normal repository pool lookup for that dependency.
expectation.conceptual: The resolver must honor explicit source requirements. A direct-origin package may be reused only when it is actually a valid match for the requested dependency, not merely when it has the same name and an allowed version.

constraints.grounded: Keep direct-origin precedence for dependencies that the direct-origin package fully satisfies. Do not let a direct-origin candidate suppress repository pool results when it fails the dependency's satisfaction rules. Preserve normal version constraint behavior and source-specific dependency behavior.
constraints.conceptual: This change should fix incorrect source selection without weakening valid direct-origin resolution or blocking normal package lookup when the direct-origin candidate is not applicable.

behavior: A same-named direct-origin package with a compatible version is no longer automatically returned for every matching dependency.
A dependency with an explicit source is not satisfied by a direct-origin package unless that package satisfies the explicit source requirement as part of the dependency match.

When a direct-origin candidate does not fully satisfy the dependency, package search falls back to the configured package pool instead of returning the direct-origin candidate or an empty result solely because a direct-origin package exists.
A direct-origin package remains eligible and preferred when it fully satisfies the dependency being resolved.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with both a direct-origin dependency and a same-named dependency that declares an explicit repository source, when resolving the explicit-source dependency, it should select a package from the requested source rather than the direct-origin package.

Given a direct-origin package whose version matches a dependency but whose source does not satisfy that dependency, when searching for packages, it should continue normal repository lookup and expose matching repository packages.

Given a dependency without an incompatible explicit source and a direct-origin package that fully satisfies it, when resolving the dependency, it should still be satisfied by the direct-origin package.

Given a direct-origin package that does not satisfy the dependency's version constraint, when resolving the dependency, it should not block discovery of compatible packages from configured repositories.

task_10.title: Respect explicit sources for direct-origin dependencies
task_10.description: Poetry 1.5.1 fixes dependency resolution for projects that declare multiple constraints for the same dependency, especially when one constraint uses a direct origin such as git, URL, file, or path and another constraint uses a version requirement tied to an explicit source repository. A previously resolved direct-origin package should only be reused when it satisfies the full dependency requirement, including source compatibility, not merely when its version matches.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution respects explicit source repositories when multiple constraints combine direct-origin dependencies with version-based dependencies.

expectation.grounded: When Provider.search_for evaluates an available direct-origin Package for a Dependency of the same name, it should return that package only when the package satisfies the dependency's name, version constraint, and source requirements. Direct-origin packages may satisfy dependencies that do not explicitly specify a source, but they must not satisfy dependencies whose source_name or source metadata requires PyPI or a named repository unless the package source is compatible. If the direct-origin package does not satisfy the dependency, resolution should continue by searching the package pool for matching repository candidates.
expectation.conceptual: A direct URL, git, file, or path dependency can be reused for an unconstrained source requirement when it is otherwise compatible, but an explicitly sourced dependency must be resolved from that requested source rather than being silently replaced by a matching direct-origin package.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress direct-origin priority for dependencies that omit an explicit source and match the package name and version constraint. Preserve rejection of direct-origin candidates whose version does not satisfy the dependency constraint. Preserve normal repository-pool lookup whenever a direct-origin candidate is absent or fails full dependency satisfaction.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing successful direct-origin workflows working, while preventing direct-origin packages from overriding a user's explicit source selection.

behavior: A cached or already resolved direct-origin package is considered a candidate only if it satisfies the dependency as a whole, including source compatibility.
A dependency without an explicit source can still be satisfied by a compatible direct-origin package with the same name and an allowed version.
A dependency with an explicit source repository is not satisfied by a URL, git, file, or path package solely because the package name and version match.
When a direct-origin package is not source-compatible or version-compatible with the dependency, the resolver searches the configured package repositories for valid candidates.

Multiple mutually exclusive constraints for the same dependency can combine direct-origin entries and version/source entries, with each environment marker selecting a package from the appropriate origin.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency declared with a direct URL, git, file, or path origin for one condition and a version requirement from an explicit repository for another condition, when the explicit-repository condition applies, it should resolve the package from the requested repository.

Given a compatible direct-origin package and a dependency requirement for the same package that does not name a source, when resolution searches for candidates, it should allow the direct-origin package to satisfy that requirement.

Given a compatible direct-origin package and a dependency requirement for the same package that explicitly names PyPI or a configured repository, when the direct-origin package is not from that source, it should not be used to satisfy the requirement.

Given a direct-origin package whose version does not satisfy a dependency's version constraint, when resolution searches for candidates, it should ignore that direct-origin package and look for repository candidates instead.
When multiple constraints for one dependency use mutually exclusive markers, resolution should choose candidates according to both the active marker and the declared source semantics.

task_12.title: Correct wheel tags for build-script packages
task_12.description: The update fixes wheel compatibility tag generation for packages that use a build script. Such wheels should be tagged for the Python executable that is actually used as the build target, not accidentally for the interpreter running Poetry or poetry-core.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that wheels built for projects with a build script receive compatibility tags that match the target build interpreter and platform, including when Poetry or poetry-core is running outside that build environment.

expectation.grounded: For build-script wheels, WheelBuilder.tag should derive the tag from the build executable associated with the builder. If that executable differs from the current process interpreter, the tag should be obtained from the target executable's supported sys tags and the first supported tag should be used. If it is the same interpreter, normal in-process packaging tag resolution should continue to be used. Non-build-script wheels should continue to use the existing pure-Python tag behavior, including the Python 2/3 universal distinction. If querying the target executable fails, callers should receive a RuntimeError with readable diagnostic output.
expectation.conceptual: Binary or platform-specific wheels should advertise compatibility with the environment they are built for, even when the build frontend itself is launched from a different Python environment. Pure-Python wheels should keep their existing universal compatibility tags.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the tag behavior for packages without a build script. Do not change wheel contents, metadata semantics, or source distribution behavior beyond the corrected wheel tag selection. In-environment build-script wheel builds should keep using the standard packaging tag calculation for the active interpreter. Failures while discovering tags from another executable should remain explicit instead of silently falling back to an unrelated interpreter tag.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to choosing the correct wheel compatibility tag and must not broaden, narrow, or silently misrepresent package compatibility.

behavior: Build-script wheel tags are no longer always based on the interpreter running Poetry or poetry-core.
When the configured build executable differs from the current process interpreter, wheel tag selection is based on that target executable's supported tags.
When the configured build executable is the current process interpreter, build-script wheel tag selection continues to use the normal in-process packaging tag calculation.
The selected build-script wheel tag is the first supported tag reported for the relevant interpreter.
Pure-Python wheel tags for packages without build scripts remain unchanged.
If the target executable cannot be queried for supported tags, tag resolution raises RuntimeError with decoded subprocess output available to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with a build script and a build executable different from the interpreter running Poetry or poetry-core, when a wheel is built, it should be named and tagged for the build executable's interpreter, ABI, and platform.

Given a project with a build script built inside the same interpreter environment as Poetry or poetry-core, when a wheel is built, it should use a valid standard compatibility tag for that active interpreter.
Given a project without a build script, when a wheel is built, it should continue to receive the existing pure-Python universal tag behavior.
When the target build executable fails while reporting supported tags, wheel tag resolution should fail explicitly with a RuntimeError rather than producing a tag for the wrong interpreter.

task_11.title: Fix recursive marker multi-constraint operations
task_11.description: The update fixes an endless recursion in marker handling by defining direct semantics for combining two multi-constraints. Intersections now merge the unique component constraints from both sides, while unions retain only the component constraints common to both sides, allowing dependency resolution and marker simplification to complete instead of failing with recursion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that marker handling can combine multiple negative environment constraints without entering endless recursion, especially when dependency resolution needs to compare or simplify two multi-constraint marker expressions.

expectation.grounded: When `MultiConstraint.intersect()` receives another `MultiConstraint`, it should return a `MultiConstraint` containing all unique component `Constraint` objects from both operands. When `MultiConstraint.union()` receives another `MultiConstraint`, it should return a `MultiConstraint` containing the component `Constraint` objects shared by both operands. Both operations should complete without raising a recursion-related runtime error.
expectation.conceptual: Combining two sets of environment marker restrictions should produce the correct simplified restriction instead of crashing. Intersection should narrow the result by requiring every distinct restriction, while union should broaden the result by keeping only restrictions that both alternatives have in common.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing `MultiConstraint` behavior for operations with a single `Constraint` and for other `BaseConstraint` implementations. The fix should be limited to the observable behavior of direct `MultiConstraint`-to-`MultiConstraint` intersection and union, without changing unrelated constraint APIs or marker semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only remove the recursion failure and define the missing combination behavior; existing marker and dependency constraint behavior outside this multi-constraint case should continue to work as before.

behavior: `MultiConstraint.intersect()` with another `MultiConstraint` returns a multi-constraint made from the unique constraints in both operands.
Duplicate component constraints shared by both operands are included only once in an intersection result.
`MultiConstraint.union()` with another `MultiConstraint` returns a multi-constraint made from the constraints present in both operands.
Partial overlap between two multi-constraints is simplified to the shared restrictions for union, rather than causing a recursion failure.
Marker normalization and dependency resolution paths that combine multi-constraint markers can finish normally instead of failing with an endless recursion.
acceptance_criteria: Given two multi-constraint marker expressions that share one restriction and each have a different additional restriction, when they are intersected, then the result should contain the shared restriction and both additional restrictions, with no duplicate for the shared restriction.

Given two multi-constraint marker expressions that share one restriction and each have a different additional restriction, when they are unioned, then the result should contain only the shared restriction.
When marker simplification or dependency resolution combines two `MultiConstraint` instances, it should complete without raising a recursion-related runtime error.
When a `MultiConstraint` is combined with a single `Constraint`, the existing intersection and union semantics for that case should remain unchanged.

task_13.title: Export explicit source index options
task_13.description: The export command now includes package sources configured with explicit priority when generating requirement file index options, so packages resolved from those sources remain installable from the exported output.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that exporting requirements includes the necessary index URL and trusted-host options for package sources configured with explicit priority.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry export` or the `Exporter` generates a requirements-style text output, any HTTP repository source with priority `explicit` that matches a locked package source URL must be considered when emitting `--extra-index-url` and, where applicable, `--trusted-host` entries.
expectation.conceptual: An exported requirements file should preserve all package source information needed for installation, including sources that are only used for explicitly assigned packages.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing export behavior for non-explicit repositories, package requirement lines, source URL matching, and trusted-host generation unchanged except that explicit-priority HTTP repositories are no longer excluded from index option generation.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only expand coverage to previously omitted explicit sources and should not alter unrelated dependency export semantics.

behavior: Explicit-priority HTTP repositories are included when the exporter matches locked package source URLs to known repositories.
A requirements export that references an explicit source emits the corresponding `--extra-index-url` entry.
For an explicit source whose host requires trust handling, the requirements export emits the corresponding `--trusted-host` entry.
Exports for packages from ordinary configured repositories continue to produce the same index options and dependency lines as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project with a locked package sourced from an explicit-priority repository, when requirements are exported, it should include the repository as an extra index URL.
Given that explicit-priority repository uses a host that requires trusted-host handling, when requirements are exported, it should include the host in trusted-host options.
When a project uses only non-explicit repositories, the exported requirements output should remain compatible with prior behavior.
When dependency lines are exported, they should remain present and unaffected by whether their source repository has explicit priority.
